what: Wired the detect_paddle.py --serve warm worker into runPaddleStage (HANDOFF_V3 §6 item 4, W2-worker-integration.md sketch). New packages/swing-lab/src/paddleWorker.ts: PaddleServeWorker (paddle-serve-v1 JSONL client: ready handshake, id-matched requests, ready/request timeouts, crash detection, dispose = stdin EOF then 3s SIGKILL backstop — lifetime tied to the parent, no orphan), startPaddleWorker (null when the venv/script is absent), detectPaddleWindow (worker-first with fallback to the legacy one-shot execFileSync path on ANY worker failure). analyzeVideo.ts spawns the worker immediately after arg parse so startup overlaps pose extraction, and disposes it in a finally around the run. Default ON (bit-equality proven, below); --no-paddle-worker restores the one-shot-only path. timings.paddleDetectViaWorker (1/0) records which path produced the artifact.

bitEquality.method: Both paths run on 2 committed dev bundle clips (wm-volley-02, afn-sasebo-rally1 — the only dev bundles with committed clip.mp4; afn-sasebo-rally2 has no committed clip; held-out clips not used), full-clip window, Linux CPU. compare_paddle_dets.py one-shot vs worker, plus a byte-compare of the serialized frames array (JSON.stringify of parsed frames).
bitEquality.sameSathRepeatability: one-shot rep1 vs rep2 frames byte-equal on both clips (CPU deterministic)
bitEquality.note: Byte-for-byte equality holds for the frames payload; the timing block differs by construction (worker requests report modelLoadSec 0.0 and their own wall/inference times). Detection content (boxes/scores/labels/tMs) is what downstream consumes and what the regen manifest hashes care about.

latencyLinuxCpu.label: LINUX-CPU (this box, torch 2.13.0+cpu, D-FINE medium via transformers 5.16.1). Explicitly NOT Mac/MPS and NOT iPhone numbers — HANDOFF_V3's 17.25s→~11.9s projection is a Mac/MPS projection and is NOT reproducible on this hardware.
latencyLinuxCpu.reading: Per-request saving on Linux CPU is ~2-4s (python import + model load removed from the request path; the 2.6s startup itself overlaps pose extraction in the wired pipeline). CPU inference (~110-125ms/frame) dominates request wall time here, so the relative win is much smaller than on Mac MPS where W2 measured 5.81s/request vs 17.1-30.4s one-shot. The wiring (not this hardware) is what the Mac projection needs.
latencyLinuxCpu.provenance: /tmp c07 harness driving PaddleServeWorker and the same execFileSync argv as runPaddleStage's fallback; raw numbers in this file are pasted from its c07-measurements.json output.

tests: packages/swing-lab/test/paddleWorker.test.ts (11 tests): protocol happy path, ok=false rejection with continued service, crash rejection, request timeout kills worker, never-ready timeout, dispose idempotent + process exit; detectPaddleWindow fallback matrix (worker success → no one-shot; error/crash/null worker → one-shot exactly once). swing-lab suite 158 passed / 4 skipped; pnpm typecheck clean (swing-lab, the only package touched).
honestNegatives: Could not run the full analyzeVideo pipeline or pnpm lab:regen on this box: pose extraction (Apple Vision) is macOS-only and canonical run dirs are absent. The ~11.9s E2E projection therefore remains UNVERIFIED — verify on the Mac by running analyze:video with and without --no-paddle-worker.
afn-sasebo-rally2 (one of W2's two Mac equality clips) has no committed clip.mp4, so equality was re-proven on afn-sasebo-rally1 instead.

Full paddle-dets.json files are NOT byte-identical across paths — the timing block records per-invocation wall/inference/load times. compare_paddle_dets.py (the W2 pass bar) and the frames byte-compare both pass.
Worker startup on this box (2.6s) is much cheaper than Mac's measured 5.5s because CPU torch import is lighter than MPS; do not transfer either number to the other platform.
blocked: Mac E2E measurement of the wired path (17.25s → projected ~11.9s) — macOS-only pose extraction; needs a Mac run of pnpm analyze:video (worker default ON) vs --no-paddle-worker.
